season_archive_entry.speaker: narrator
season_archive_entry.text: By late spring, the paper fish had begun to curl. They hung from the copying annex's lintel, folded by a child who had expected visitors to mistake them for swallows. Lin Yue paused beneath them with a notice held flat against her satchel. The annex would lose its lease after the autumn market unless another arrangement could be made. Inside, someone was laughing at a spilled cup. The laugh made the threatened room seem less like a cause and more like a place that people were already using.

season_archive_m01_002.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_002.text: Su Yao sat behind a table whose legs had been wedged with ordinary wooden scraps. Her ivory and teal robe had a repaired cuff, the repair's thread slightly darker than the cloth. She greeted Yue and moved a stack of empty sleeves away from the near chair. 'You can see the problem before deciding whether to help,' she said. The offer suited Yue better than a speech about duty. She set her own satchel down without letting its strap pull at the affected shoulder and looked around the small room.

season_archive_m01_003.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_003.text: The annex was a leased copying room attached to the archive's ordinary public work. Its shelves held approved copies, blank paper and records waiting within named permissions. The archive itself was not being abolished. The room's owner wanted the annex back for storage after autumn; other rooms remained in use, though none could simply absorb everything here. Su indicated the damp bottom corner of one wall. 'Even an extension would not mend that,' she said. Yue had expected one threat and found two kinds of time running against each other.

season_archive_m01_004.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_004.text: Qiu Lian emerged from behind a shelf carrying an empty board at waist height. Her black braid had a pale thread caught near its end. She set the board down before speaking. 'The notice makes it sound as though the lease is our only enemy.' Yue looked at the wall. 'You prefer an enemy that can be replaced with a better joint.' Qiu's mouth moved toward a smile and stopped. Their previous encounters had established whatever their own chosen records supported. This room offered a new question without requiring either woman to pretend they had become close.

season_archive_m01_005.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_005.text: Su showed them the room's actual scope. The current project concerned a group of ordinary household and trade records offered for preservation copying under their owners' permissions. Some were already public; others were limited to named sections. A sealed packet of Echo memories occupied a different locked cabinet and lay outside the project entirely. Neither woman would read it, infer its contents or make its unavailability sound like guilt. 'The room is full of enough human trouble without borrowing a hidden mind,' Qiu said. Yue appreciated the plain sentence.

season_archive_m01_006.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_006.text: The project had its own owner-supported space and material account, separate from the completed trial's grant. That earlier pouch and its three afternoons were closed facts. Su was not extending them by changing the name of the table. Yue could offer only newly verified available intervals around existing accepted work. Qiu had her own obligations. They would decide any bounded copying role after seeing the papers and the handling arrangements. Nobody acquired a specialist qualification by caring about a threatened room.

season_archive_m01_007.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_007.text: A clerk brought a shallow tray from the approved intake shelf and placed it on the table's far side. Yue did not have to lift it. Inside lay a laundry book with a split cover, two folded delivery sheets and a small strip of cloth bearing three faded red marks. A paper label called the contents South-bank household papers. Beneath that label, a second label had been partly torn away. The missing half left the first stroke of a place name and a date that could have belonged to either of two years.

season_archive_m01_008.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_008.text: Qiu leaned close enough to see without touching the cloth. 'There is our attractive mystery,' she said. Yue asked why attractive. 'Because people will want the missing half to contain the only interesting thing.' Su drew the permissions sheet alongside the tray. The cloth's owners had approved its ordinary surface description and copying of the surviving public labels. The absent provenance strip could not be reconstructed from an appealing story. They could inspect what remained, ask authorized questions and leave an honest gap where no source had yet supplied an answer.

season_archive_m01_009.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_009.text: Yue opened the permission sheet with her good hand while Su held its far edge flat. The named household had deposited the laundry book and the public delivery sheets together. The cloth had arrived in the same outer wrapper, but its origin was not explained on the surviving intake page. The sheet's final line authorized preservation description of the group, not a claim that every object had the same maker or journey. Yue read that line aloud. Qiu answered, 'That is the difference someone will forget as soon as we give the group a neat title.'

season_archive_m01_010.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_010.text: A woman waiting at the doorway said the red marks must be a ferry seal. Her grandmother had kept something similar. Qiu thanked her for the possibility and asked whether she had brought the older example or a permitted copy. She had not. Yue said they could record her suggestion as a suggestion if she wished, without treating it as an identification. The woman laughed at the formality, then considered the cloth again. 'No, leave me out. I came to return a bowl.' Su accepted the bowl and left the suggestion unclaimed.

season_archive_m01_011.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_011.text: The room smelled of dry reed mats, ink and a faint sourness from the damp wall. Yue found a comfortable chair position with her arm supported and her working hand near the paper edge. Qiu checked that a low tray could slide between them without crossing a moving person's path. The small arrangements recalled earlier work without proving that any unchosen earlier method had occurred. This time there was no contest score. There were pages that might outlast their readers and a room whose lease could end before the copying did.

season_archive_m01_012.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_012.text: Su brought the annex's calendar. The first available work interval was the following morning, between Yue's own accepted obligations, and Qiu could attend only its latter portion. Su did not ask Yue to cancel something she had already promised. Their potential task was ordinary transcription and surface description under the named permissions; trained staff would retain responsibility for the originals' care. Yue asked for a stopping point that would not leave a loose book exposed. Qiu asked for a useful product even if the last bell ended a sentence.

season_archive_m01_013.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_013.text: They wrote a modest first task: prepare a readable inventory of the authorized group, copy one already approved public sheet and identify questions that required an owner response. The task did not grant permission for the whole laundry book. Su would obtain any further section approval before it became a copying object. Qiu looked at the public sheet's neat columns. 'That can leave here usefully tomorrow,' she said. Yue looked at the torn label. 'And this can leave here falsely tomorrow if we make the title do more than the inventory.'

season_archive_m01_014.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_014.text: Beyond the window, a cart paused while its driver argued with a child about a sleeping dog. The dog occupied the warmest patch of road and showed no interest in the lease. Qiu watched the dispute through the open shutter. 'A room can spend a week deciding where to put a table while the good light moves every hour,' she said. Yue replied that a rushed table could force a copier's shoulder into the same bad angle every day. Qiu looked at the near chair and moved the paper rest inward without making a performance of concession.

season_archive_m01_015.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_015.text: The approved public sheet described deliveries of soap ash and cloth to several households. It did not describe a rescue, a battle or a secret lineage. Yue liked its stubborn ordinariness. A line could matter because someone had needed clean clothing, paid for soap and remembered a debt. Qiu pointed to a crossed quantity. The correction had been signed in a different hand. Even a plain delivery sheet contained a small drama: somebody had challenged a number and somebody else had agreed to let the challenge remain visible.

season_archive_m01_016.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_016.text: Yue copied the line's shape onto a scrap without yet making a project copy. Her good hand stayed close to the table, and she paused before the sustained position became tiring. Qiu said the correction signature's last stroke looked like a numeral. Yue held the scrap farther into the light. It could be one, but the surrounding ink made that uncertain. They would describe a crossed quantity with a signed correction, leaving the exact signature interpretation open. The sheet had not asked them to turn every stroke into a person.

season_archive_m01_017.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_017.text: Su took them to the consent room to show how owner responses would arrive. They would be kept beside the project index with their stated limits, not silently absorbed into broad permission. An owner could approve a recipe page while declining a household dispute on its reverse. Qiu said two sides of one leaf made a difficult physical boundary. Su agreed. Staff could shield or present the approved side; a copier did not get the refused side as a bonus for being nearby. Yue noticed how firmly Qiu accepted that answer.

season_archive_m01_018.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_018.text: The consent room had a low bench and a window facing a courtyard where someone had planted beans in cracked pots. Yue sat while Su fetched the forms. Qiu stood beside a pot whose vine had reached a broken lattice. 'It has chosen the worst support,' she said. Su replied that the gardener would fix the lattice before blaming the vine. Yue laughed, and Qiu turned with a slight look of surprise. A joke could cross a room more easily than an argument, provided nobody demanded it prove a warmer relationship than existed.

season_archive_m01_019.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_019.text: The owner of the annex passed the courtyard carrying a measuring stick. She greeted Su politely and asked whether she had considered the storage shelves she would need after autumn. She was not a villain stealing the archive's memory. She had a business whose goods currently stood in a rented shed, and the shed's owner wanted it back. The displacement continued beyond this room. Su asked for the written dimensions of her proposed shelves. She promised to bring them. Qiu watched her go without offering a speech that made her own need the only real one.

season_archive_m01_020.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_020.text: Yue asked whether the project's threatened lease was being used to hurry owners into broader consent. Su's face grew serious. 'It must not be,' she said. The autumn deadline could limit what the annex completed; it could not make a household's private paper public by impatience. Qiu asked whether they would have to return an incomplete book if permission remained narrow. Su said yes. Incompletion was a possible honest result. The answer frustrated Qiu, but she did not turn frustration into an accusation against the absent owner.

season_archive_m01_021.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_021.text: They returned to the copying room and found the paper fish on the lintel swinging in a warm draft. A child beneath them insisted that one was now a crane because its tail had changed shape. Qiu asked what the maker had intended. 'A fish,' the child said, 'but it can become a crane.' Yue looked at the torn provenance label and felt the temptation of that freedom in the wrong place. An invented creature could change its name without injury. An inherited object required a source before a reader changed its history.

season_archive_m01_022.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_022.text: Su let the child choose a new name for the paper creature and asked him not to relabel the project tray. The distinction amused him. He promised, then asked whether the cloth strip had ever been a flag. Qiu said they did not know. He was disappointed for a breath and then wanted to know what they could see. Three red marks, a frayed edge, a folded crease and a label with a missing half. Yue found that list more inviting than she expected. An honest surface still offered enough for curiosity.

season_archive_m01_023.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_023.text: Qiu laid a blank inventory card beside the tray. She wanted the heading to identify the group quickly. Yue proposed Authorized household and delivery papers, with unresolved cloth provenance. Qiu said that title would use half the card. Su suggested a short group number for handling and a full descriptive heading beneath it. The short identifier would not become the history. They agreed, and the disagreement produced a practical arrangement without forcing either author to renounce her preference for brevity or limits.

season_archive_m01_024.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_024.text: The clerk who had brought the tray returned to ask whether it could go back before closing. Yue had nearly forgotten how easily a discussion held an original out longer than necessary. They finished the preliminary view and let the clerk return it to the approved shelf. Qiu marked the actual items seen on their planning scrap. Their first work morning would begin with the same group only if staff presented it again under the permissions then in force. Tonight's enthusiasm could not keep a fragile book on a table after its responsible keeper needed to put it away.

season_archive_m01_025.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_025.text: On the way to the kitchen, Yue noticed the annex owner's measuring stick leaning beside the entrance. Someone had tied a red thread around its middle so it would not be mistaken for a shelf strip. Qiu saw her glance. 'There is another red mark asking to become a mystery,' she said. Yue answered that this one had a living owner within calling distance. Qiu smiled. Asking the owner was sometimes quicker than inventing a history, and sometimes the owner could answer only part. They would find out which kind of case their cloth was.

season_archive_m01_026.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_026.text: The shared kitchen's cook had made noodles thin enough to catch on a spoon. Su asked before taking bowls from the ready stack. The meal belonged to the ordinary kitchen arrangement, not to the closed trial grant or an invented project reward. Yue chose a place against the wall, Qiu took the opposite stool and Su sat at the table end. For several minutes their concerns shrank to warm broth, spring onions and whether the cook had used too much pepper. It was possible to love a room most clearly when nothing ceremonial happened in it.

season_archive_m01_027.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_027.text: Qiu said the annex threatened to become a museum of unfinished questions. Yue asked whether a finished false answer would be better. Qiu set down her spoon. 'You hear finished and supply false too quickly.' Yue recognized the rebuke. She asked what Qiu wanted finished first. 'The sheet we can already read and already copy,' Qiu said. 'Something a person can use before autumn.' Yue could agree with the desire while still worrying about the unresolved heading. Neither concern needed to erase the other.

season_archive_m01_028.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_028.text: Su admitted that she had been telling supporters about the red-marked cloth because it made them listen. The plain soap deliveries drew less attention. Yue asked whether she had described the missing label as a mystery. 'A missing source,' Su said, then sighed. 'Sometimes I said mystery.' Qiu looked toward the kitchen shelf. 'Then the annex has already begun selling the question.' Su did not defend the word. She would use missing source in future explanations and correct a specific inflated account if it returned. The room's need for help did not make suspense harmless.

season_archive_m01_029.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_029.text: A man at the next table heard the last sentence and asked what cloth they meant. Su gave him the limited public description without reciting household names. He said his cousin knew every old ferry mark in the valley. Qiu asked whether the cousin would be willing to examine a permitted surface copy if the project supplied one. The man shrugged. 'I mostly meant that he talks as though he does.' They laughed. An apparent expert could dissolve into an ordinary cousin before anyone built a task around his authority.

season_archive_m01_030.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_030.text: Yue watched Qiu tear a noodle with the edge of her spoon and thought about the copying morning. A public sheet, a group inventory and an unresolved source question could each absorb the short interval. Beginning with one would postpone another. Su could keep the objects safe, but she could not make time multiply. The choice needed to name what they would actually prioritize, not award care or efficiency an abstract victory. Qiu noticed her thinking and said, 'Choose the work, then let me argue about how to do it.'

season_archive_m01_031.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_031.text: After supper, they returned to the annex doorway to confirm the first morning's scope. Yue accepted the bounded ordinary copying role within her verified free interval. Qiu accepted a separately stated later portion. Staff would handle originals and retain preservation responsibility; the authors would transcribe and describe approved surfaces only. Any added task or conflicted date would need its own agreement. The room's separate material provision covered the planned paper and ink. No wage, advance, qualification or cultivation growth appeared merely because two women signed a modest work page.

season_archive_m01_032.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_032.text: Su showed them three possible priorities within that one available morning. They could first examine the surviving provenance words and prepare a precise owner question, accepting fewer completed copies. They could finish the already clear public delivery sheet first, accepting that its group heading would carry an explicit unresolved cloth note. Or they could request a narrower owner-approved inventory before further copying, accepting a slower start and reducing the chance that a handling group became a provenance claim. Each choice would leave other work for later actual intervals.

season_archive_m01_033.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_033.text: Qiu wanted the public sheet first. Yue wanted to know whether the missing strip's surviving year could be copied without inventing its last digit. Su refused to break the tie by appealing to the lease. 'Autumn is a boundary, not a witness,' she said. The sentence pleased Yue until she saw Qiu's expression. Qiu had not been asking autumn to prove a date; she had been asking them to produce something before it. Yue acknowledged that distinction. The disagreement stayed useful because the women corrected the account of each other's motives.

season_archive_m01_034.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_034.text: The paper fish above them had flattened as the evening air cooled. Yue touched none of the originals before choosing. She stood with her satchel supported close to her body and her affected shoulder comfortable. Qiu leaned against the doorframe, waiting with obvious effort. Su held the work page low between them. Beyond the courtyard, the annex owner's cart rolled toward her other shed. The threatened room belonged to an ordinary network of people whose needs would not vanish because the copying project had found a compelling question.

season_archive_m01_priority.speaker: lin_yue
season_archive_m01_priority.text: Yue chose the first copying morning's actual priority. A surviving-source question could prevent a neat heading from outrunning its evidence. A completed authorized sheet could make the threatened room useful now. A narrower owner-approved inventory could place a clearer boundary around the group before copying expanded. The interval would not contain all three. Each priority preserved the sealed packet's exclusion, the staff's responsibility for originals and the existing calendar; each would leave a different piece of unfinished work.

choices.text: Examine the surviving provenance words first and prepare a precise owner question.
Finish the already authorized public delivery sheet first, with its unresolved group note.
Prepare a narrower inventory for the owner's approval before expanding the copying.

season_archive_m01_source_001.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_001.text: The following morning arrived warm and misty. Yue reached the annex within the accepted interval and found Su holding the approved tray near the window. They began with the surviving provenance label rather than the full delivery sheet. Yue could see the first two year strokes clearly, the third partly and the final place where the paper had torn. She copied the visible strokes as shapes on a descriptive scrap. An exact year remained unwritten. Su placed the scrap beside the original so the missing portion could be seen.

season_archive_m01_source_002.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_002.text: Qiu arrived at her stated later time and found only three lines on Yue's page. Her disappointment was immediate. 'You have made the absence very handsome,' she said. Yue moved the scrap into the light. 'I have made it inspectable.' Qiu looked, then admitted the third stroke was less clear than it had seemed yesterday. She wanted to call it a seven. Yue asked her to draw the possible seven and the other shape she could see. The two drawings looked unpleasantly similar. They kept both as possibilities, not competing dates.

season_archive_m01_source_003.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_003.text: The torn edge had folded under the surviving paper. Staff lifted it under the ordinary handling procedure while the two copiers watched. No lost half appeared. A tiny ink point on the underside belonged to the visible stroke's continuation, not a hidden name. Qiu laughed softly at her own eagerness. 'For a moment I wanted the paper to reward us.' Yue answered that paper had no obligation to stage a reveal. The observation still mattered: their descriptive copy now showed the folded edge as staff had presented it.

season_archive_m01_source_004.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_004.text: Together they wrote an owner question naming the authorized group, the surviving label and the uncertainty. It asked whether the owner retained a permitted source explaining the cloth's arrival, or remembered who had supplied the missing strip. It did not ask for the sealed Echo packet. It offered room for no answer, partial answer or refusal. Qiu trimmed a paragraph about the annex's lease because it could make an ordinary request feel like pressure. Yue accepted the cut. The useful short question owed some of its precision to what they chose not to invoke.

season_archive_m01_source_005.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_005.text: Su checked the question against the project's permissions and agreed to send it through the ordinary owner contact already on file. Sending the question would not turn an unreceived reply into evidence. The task page named the surviving strokes copied, the uncertain year and the owner question prepared. They had not completed the whole public delivery sheet. Qiu added that fact in a plain line. The morning had produced a careful beginning rather than a finished item that a visitor could immediately take away.

season_archive_m01_source_006.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_006.text: With the remaining minutes, Yue copied the public sheet's first heading and one clear line as a practice section, marked incomplete. Qiu watched the ink dry without pretending that a single line was the promised finished sheet. She pointed out that the correction signature might be copied more clearly if the paper rest shifted a little. Yue tried the low adjustment and found it comfortable. Their source-first choice had still allowed a small practical improvement. The improvement did not pay back the lost quantity or make the full copy exist.

season_archive_m01_source_007.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_007.text: A visitor asked whether the new scrap had solved the old date. Qiu answered no before Yue could speak. It showed the surviving marks more clearly and left the last digit missing. The visitor said a date with a question mark looked less impressive on an exhibit card. Yue agreed that uncertainty could disappoint an audience. Qiu asked what impressive date he wanted to write without a source. He shrugged and looked again. Their first public explanation had preserved the actual source-first work instead of selling its carefulness as a discovery.

season_archive_m01_source_008.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_source_008.text: At the agreed stopping point, staff returned the original tray to its shelf. Yue and Qiu kept the approved descriptive work and unfinished practice section within the project folder. The route left a precise owner question awaiting an actual response and the full public-sheet copy still unfinished. Qiu said she would remember the morning as useful and frustrating. Yue said that was accurate. They went to the courtyard with the page's small visible uncertainties intact, having chosen a source question over a larger finished copy.

season_archive_m01_copy_001.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_001.text: The following morning, Yue began with the authorized public delivery sheet. Staff presented it on the low support, and Su laid out clean paper within Yue's comfortable reach. The group's inventory heading carried the explicit unresolved cloth note. Yue copied the soap ash entries and the signed crossed quantity, leaving the correction visible. She did not turn the sheet into a story about the cloth merely because they had arrived in the same outer wrapper. The ordinary deliveries could become useful copies on their own evidence.

season_archive_m01_copy_002.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_002.text: Qiu arrived during the second column and examined the first page without praising its speed. She found a copied number whose closing stroke resembled a different digit. Yue looked back at the presented original. Her copy had compressed the space too tightly. She redrew the line cleanly and marked the discarded draft as superseded. Qiu said this was the sort of delay she wanted counted honestly: a finished sheet needed more than a quick hand. Yue agreed and kept copying without turning the correction into an argument against the chosen priority.

season_archive_m01_copy_003.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_003.text: The signed crossed quantity required more room than a neat copyist's instinct would have given it. Qiu proposed reproducing the crossed figure beside the accepted figure rather than hiding the crossing in a note. Su confirmed that the authorized surface copy could preserve both visible states. Yue placed them as shown and added a brief descriptive line about the signature's unclear final stroke. The result was readable without improving the original into a perfect account. Qiu liked the page because it could travel; Yue liked it because its trouble traveled with it.

season_archive_m01_copy_004.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_004.text: At the midpoint, they checked the copied households against the authorized public names on the sheet. One line had been shielded under the owner's retained limit and remained uncopied. Yue left a named omission rather than guessing which household occupied the gap. Qiu asked whether the public copy needed an empty line at the same location. They chose a small bracket showing a withheld section, distinct from physical loss. Missing permission and missing paper were different conditions. The finished copy would keep that distinction available to a later reader.

season_archive_m01_copy_005.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_005.text: By the final portion of the interval, the clear authorized sections were copied and checked. Staff confirmed that the copied surfaces matched the approved presentation. Yue and Qiu signed their respective transcription and checking roles without calling either one a preservation specialist. The project folder received a completed bounded copy of the delivery sheet. The cloth's exact year and origin remained unresolved. They had not prepared the detailed owner question that Yue had considered yesterday. A useful finished item could stand beside an unfinished source problem without pretending to solve it.

season_archive_m01_copy_006.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_006.text: Su showed the copy to a woman researching ordinary household costs from the public shelves. She could read the soap quantities and the signed correction, and she understood the withheld-section bracket after one explanation. The woman had no interest in the red cloth. Qiu looked pleased, then almost defensive about the pleasure. Yue felt glad too. The room's usefulness did not depend on every visitor wanting its most attractive mystery. A plain sheet could answer an ordinary question and justify the morning without enlarging its claim.

season_archive_m01_copy_007.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_007.text: The woman asked whether the missing provenance label changed the delivery figures. Yue answered that the figures were copied from the identified authorized sheet, while the cloth's origin belonged to a separate unresolved description. Qiu pointed to the distinct headings. The answer was easier because they had refused to give the whole wrapper one confident history. The visitor copied a permitted line into her own notebook and thanked them. Their sheet-first choice had made an actual usable item, and its careful boundary had prevented that usefulness from spreading too far.

season_archive_m01_copy_008.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_copy_008.text: At the agreed stopping point, staff returned the originals to their shelf and Su filed the completed approved copy. Yue rested her shoulder before rising. Qiu said, 'This is the morning I wanted: somebody could use the work before we solved everything.' Yue replied, 'And somebody could see what it didn't solve.' The route left the provenance question for a later actual interval, with no detailed owner request yet prepared. They carried the pleasure of a finished limited page into the courtyard without inventing a finished group history.

season_archive_m01_owner_001.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_001.text: The following morning, Yue began a narrower inventory intended for owner approval. Staff presented the tray without expanding the current permission, and Su supplied the existing handling identifier. Yue listed the laundry book, public delivery sheets and red-marked cloth as separately described objects within one received wrapper. She left the group's provenance heading provisional. The work did not copy the private portions of the book. It asked the owner to confirm which objects and sections the project could describe together before a larger account went out.

season_archive_m01_owner_002.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_002.text: Qiu arrived later and found the inventory full of distinctions. 'This could become three trays and no work,' she said. Yue asked which distinction she would remove. Qiu pointed at the repeated outer-wrapper note, then saw why the cloth needed it. She crossed out one redundant phrase while preserving the relation. The narrower inventory became easier to read without pretending the objects shared a proven origin. Qiu's impatient eye could improve a boundary document, provided the boundary was allowed to remain more important than its prettiness.

season_archive_m01_owner_003.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_003.text: Su checked that the inventory request would go to the named owner through the project's ordinary contact. It would ask for approval, clarification or a retained limit, not assume silence meant consent. The owner could confirm the physical group while leaving the cloth's history unresolved. Yue liked that separation. Qiu said the reply might take longer than the remaining copy work would have taken. Both statements were true. Their chosen priority accepted the delay because the proposed public inventory risked carrying a broader claim than the current permission supported.

season_archive_m01_owner_004.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_004.text: The laundry book's split cover prompted another practical question. Its title could be copied from the approved visible front, but its inner household notes remained outside the present task. Staff showed the cover only. Yue drew the split and copied the title exactly where readable. Qiu suggested a separate condition line so a future reader would not mistake the broken cover for a missing historical year. The inventory now identified what was physically damaged and what was withheld. Neither absence became an accusation against the household.

season_archive_m01_owner_005.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_005.text: With the clearer list prepared, Qiu wanted to begin the public sheet anyway. Su checked the remaining interval and said they could copy a short heading as preparation, but not promise completion. Yue chose to leave the actual sheet work for a fresh accepted interval rather than open it into a hurried stop. Qiu disliked the decision and said so. They recorded no sheet copy this morning. The refusal preserved a tidy ending at the cost of an ordinary useful page that might have been started. Their account kept that cost visible.

season_archive_m01_owner_006.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_006.text: The request page offered the owner choices in plain language. They could approve the described grouping, correct its contents or retain a narrower section limit. Qiu removed a sentence implying that a broader approval would rescue the annex. Yue approved the removal. A room threatened by a lease had no right to use its own distress as an argument over someone else's household papers. Su signed only her role in carrying the request. The owner had not yet answered, and the project would not credit itself with consent merely for asking well.

season_archive_m01_owner_007.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_007.text: A visitor at the doorway asked whether the absence of a completed copy meant the women had done nothing. Qiu looked at the finished request and answered that they had defined a question whose answer could change the public description. Yue added that the copying quantity was still zero for the sheet. The two parts belonged together. The visitor seemed unconvinced, but Su did not flatter the route as unquestionably best. Its usefulness would depend partly on an actual owner response, which might confirm little or arrive too late for the annex's deadline.

season_archive_m01_owner_008.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_owner_008.text: At the stopping point, staff returned the tray and Su filed the request beside the present limits. Yue and Qiu had prepared a bounded inventory proposal and copied only its authorized visible cover description. The public delivery sheet remained unperformed. The owner approval remained pending. Qiu said she hoped the careful start would earn something beyond another careful start. Yue could not promise it. They left the room with a precise request, a real delay and a clearer distinction between the objects they could handle together and the history they could claim.

season_archive_m01_after_001.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_001.text: The courtyard had warmed while the women worked. The bean vine in the cracked pot had reached a new crosspiece someone had tied to the lattice. Qiu noticed it first and called it a successful intervention. Yue asked whether the vine had agreed. Qiu laughed. 'You can leave the consent joke there. It is a plant.' Yue liked the permission to stop qualifying. The morning's actual priority stayed in the folder; their conversation could be ordinary for a few breaths without making either woman careless about the work.

season_archive_m01_after_002.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_002.text: Su brought the annex owner's shelf dimensions into the courtyard. The storage plan would occupy the copying room's far wall and most of its center. There was no hidden cruelty in the drawing, only a shape incompatible with the current tables. Qiu ran a finger above the paper without marking it. 'An extension might leave us a corner,' she said. Su answered that a corner could be discussed, but nothing had been agreed. Yue looked at the beam of sunlight crossing the bench and wondered how much of a room's life could survive as a corner.

season_archive_m01_after_003.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_003.text: The owner had written a note below the dimensions: she would consider a short overlap if the copying group moved its shelves by a certain date. Su read it as an offer to discuss, not an accepted extension. Qiu wanted to inspect the proposed overlap immediately. Yue asked whether its wall was the damp one. It was. A corner that let the project stay might make its papers less safe. Su folded the plan. They needed another room survey by responsible staff before treating the offer as relief.

season_archive_m01_after_004.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_004.text: The archive's ordinary keeper came through carrying keys and a basket of empty book ties. She said the annex's damp wall had been reported, and staff would inspect it before the next wet spell. Yue did not offer to diagnose masonry. Qiu asked whether their approved copies could remain in the drier cabinet in the meantime. The keeper said she would decide after checking capacity. The answer was neither rejection nor a free transfer. The project had to fit within a working archive whose other people's materials already occupied real space.

season_archive_m01_after_005.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_005.text: Qiu looked tired when the keeper left. 'Everything here asks someone who is busy elsewhere,' she said. Yue answered that the room was not the whole institution. Qiu nodded impatiently. 'I know. I am describing why a small project can die without anyone choosing to kill it.' The sentence stayed with Yue. Neglect could be distributed among reasonable limits, each one defensible alone. That did not entitle the women to break a limit, but it gave them a reason to make the project's actual need clear enough that someone could choose it consciously.

season_archive_m01_after_006.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_006.text: At the kitchen, the cook asked whether they had solved the cloth. Qiu said they had begun the work they actually chose, with its remaining questions intact. Yue gave the cook the plain public description without making him listen to the whole permission history. He said red cloth reminded him of festival sleeves. Qiu smiled and let the association remain a kitchen thought. Not every offered memory needed to become a project lead. Sometimes a person was simply comparing a thing in front of him with a thing he liked.

season_archive_m01_after_007.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_007.text: The cook's sister was repairing a basket near the door. She said the room lease notice had worried people because the annex held copies they used to settle everyday quarrels. A vanished sheet could make the loudest neighbor sound right by default. Yue asked which copies she meant. The woman pointed to the ordinary public shelf list, not the limited household tray. Su promised to check that list when arranging any move. The preservation project and the annex's existing public service overlapped, but they were not the same bundle of papers.

season_archive_m01_after_008.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_008.text: They walked back to the copying room to look at that shelf list. It named household account copies, trade notices and public delivery summaries already available under existing permissions. Qiu said those sheets would be less likely to interest a sponsor than the red marks. Yue agreed. They were also more immediately useful to people who had never heard the word provenance. Su drew a separate relocation line for the existing public shelf. The new project would not rescue its own attractive objects by quietly letting the ordinary service vanish behind them.

season_archive_m01_after_009.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_009.text: Before leaving, Yue checked the comfortable chair position for the next accepted interval. Qiu moved the paper rest only after asking, because the low arrangement had become part of the actual working conditions. They did not reserve more days merely because the room's threats had multiplied. Su would circulate available times and owners' responses as they arrived. Yue's earlier promises remained in force. Qiu's accepted work elsewhere remained in force. A project could matter deeply without obtaining the right to consume every free hour its volunteers possessed.

season_archive_m01_after_010.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_010.text: The child who had renamed his paper fish appeared with a second folded creature. He gave it to Su, saying this one was definitely a swallow because it had never been a fish. Qiu asked whether he had written that on the back. He had. Yue turned the paper over with his permission and found an emphatic crooked word. The makers laughed together. They could enjoy a source whose author stood in the doorway and still remember the cloth whose author did not. The child pinned his new swallow beside the old uncertain creature.

season_archive_m01_after_011.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_011.text: Su closed the room for the day. Its approved work rested within the limits actually selected, its pending questions stayed pending and its sealed Echo cabinet remained untouched. The annex's separate provisions covered the planned materials; the expired trial grant had supplied none of them. Yue had used her accepted ordinary copying interval without earning a new cultivation stage or claiming staff preservation authority. Qiu had contributed the portion she accepted. Their new season began with enough useful friction to make the threatened room feel worth returning to.

season_archive_m01_after_012.speaker: narrator
season_archive_m01_after_012.text: The following week would bring an ordinary owner contact and a newly presented part of the authorized group. Before that work began, Su would read the priority record from this first morning. What they had copied, questioned or left unperformed would remain specific to their actual choice. Yue left beneath the paper creatures with a stronger sense of the annex's people and no solved cloth history. The lease still ended after autumn unless a new agreement was reached. A missing source still required a source, however much everyone wanted the room to survive.
